title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
summary: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family.
